chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Chur

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
A state of instruction and preparation is like a receptive outward mind made ready for implantation. Into such a receptivity a ministering Divine influence sets a living perception of good. Once implanted, that perception reorganizes the whole strength and quality of the external life, and from that reordering it brings forth deeds that are genuinely good. When this living good has been established in tranquility, the inmost life is set in peace, and the Divine operation rests in the accomplished use.

In the same way, a living consciousness that is now held in confused conjunction with lower things desires to be raised into the communion where its own goods and truths belong; yet it perceives that no passage stands open anywhere in the full range of its faculties, because disordered powers press upon it and constrain it on every side. No opening is found except through the paired illuminations that give discernment and make understanding shine, and in that illumination it is granted a quiet dwelling. Through this ordered light a passage is formed at the moment of emergence, and by it the consciousness is led out of confusion into its own homeland of kindred life.

Yet even these illuminations find no settled repose within the intermediate powers themselves, but only in the inmost state of pure enlightenment, which has been their own eternally.

So the living consciousness is cleansed from every distress born of disorder; interior quiet is provided; and a genuine entrance is opened into the communion of its own life.

And that inmost state of pure enlightenment becomes the final recipient of all true illumination, where it rests and exercises lasting governance, because it remains conjoined to its origin in unending order.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual progression: preparation → implantation of living good → struggle of consciousness in constraint → release through ordered illumination → rest only in the inmost enlightened state. The voice remains consistent; the only pressure-point is committing the paired ‘light-givers’ to a specific dual illumination, but it integrates smoothly with the chapter’s movement.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential simile: catechumens ↔ prepared earth; gardener ↔ planter; tree ↔ implanted life; fruit ↔ works. No narrative break; the spiritual reading can derive meaning by function (preparation, implantation, transformation, fruit-bearing, rest).
findings.evidence: Text teaches by organic function: “assembly of catechumens … like good earth … gardener shall plant … tree transforms the power and the quality of all earth, and it produces good fruit … sets at ease the tree of life, and he rests.” The Stage 3a notes explicitly say this required (and sustained) a functional translation (“preparation as receptivity … implanted good … brings forth deeds … rests in accomplished use”) with no stumble points.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential liberation sequence expressed in cosmological imagery. While “sun and moon” could invite later administrative/systematic cosmology, here they function as the only “open door” and “place of rest,” i.e., a functional passageway motif. No intrusive roster of rulers, stations, or jurisdictions; no seam connective introducing a different didactic mode.
findings.evidence: The passage is driven by states and functions: the soul is “set in mixture,” “wishes to ascend,” finds “no open door” because powers “bind” it; “except the sun and the moon … whereby they become the place of rest … a door that opens … comes out through them.” The spiritual reading’s only ‘pressure-point’ is interpretive specificity (“paired illuminations”), but it reports it “integrates smoothly,” which is consistent with a stable substrate rather than an insertion.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation, not an overlay: it tightens the ‘rest’ motif by relocating it from intermediate powers to the ultimate ‘land of light.’ Still correspondential (rest-place logic), not administrative (no governance hierarchy).
findings.evidence: “Light-givers … have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the land of light.” This is an intensification of the functional claim in ¶7 (“place of rest … door”). Stage 3a notes: “SHIFTS inward, locating true rest not in intermediates but in the inmost,” indicating narrative continuity rather than disruption.

findings.diagnosis: Clean summarizing consequence: purification → rest provided → door opened. This is the expected resolution of ¶7–8 and contains no foreign teaching mode.
findings.evidence: “So, thus the living soul is purified … they provide a rest for it, and open a door … to the house of its people.” Stage 3a: “Clean translation; no major resistances.” The internal logic (‘rest/door/house of its people’) is exactly the thread established earlier.

findings.diagnosis: Minor mixed-voice coloration: “rule … for ever” introduces governance language, but it is embedded as a concluding stability claim about the final resting-place of the light-givers, not a jurisdictional inventory. It reads as an eschatological completion of the rest-motif, not an administrative insertion.
findings.evidence: “Land of light will become the final receiver … they will rest themselves therein and rule in it for ever.” The chapter’s core vocabulary is ‘rest/place/door/house’; “final receiver” and “rest … for ever” continue that functional arc. The spiritual reading did not stumble here, treating “rule” as “lasting governance” within the same progression; there is no sudden appearance of named officials, stations, or ranked lists that would signal Mani’s administrative layer.

textual_criticism.summary: No textual disruptions detected. All paragraphs form a coherent correspondential narrative (preparation → implantation → constraint in mixture → exit through the light-givers → rest only in the land of light). ¶10 contains slight administrative coloration (“rule for ever”) but not enough to indicate an insertion or overlay; it functions as a normal concluding stabilization. Recommended excisions: 0. Recommended annotations: 0.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: What does the assembly of catechu[me]ns resemble? It is like good earth [made ready] in which the gardener shall plant a good tree. [Beho]ld, [th]at good tree transforms the power and the [quality] of all earth, and it produces good fruit. [Th]at [gardener] sets at ease the tree of life, and he r[ests himself].

Likewise this [liv]ing sou[l] that today is set in mixture; for it wishes to [as]cend and go to the house of its people, but it kn[ow[s a]]nd understands that it has no open door in all the powers of heaven and earth. For they are its oppression that [binds] it everywhere. Indeed, it has no open door except the sun and the moon themselves, the light-givers of the heavens [whereby] they become the place of rest for it. And they become a door that opens for it [in] the coming forth, and (the soul) comes out through them to the country of the household of i[ts] people.
Again, further in, also the light-givers of the heavens have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the lan[d] of light, that has indeed been theirs for ever.
So, thus the living soul is purified of all afflictions; and they provide a rest for it, and open a door that opens to the house [of] its people.
Also, it is the case that the land of lig[ht] will become the final receiver for the light-givers of [the] heavens, and they will rest themselves therein and rule in it [for] ever.
